name: Distracted Boyfriend
scene: A man walking with his girlfriend turns to ogle another woman. Three labels: original loyalty (slot 0), new shiny distraction (slot 1), the man being tempted (slot 2).
when: User is abandoning something sensible they have for a shinier new obsession. Pattern: existing thing → new shiny thing → the user/themself.

example.user_said: I'm rewriting our working Node auth in Rust because I'm bored.

name: Drakeposting
scene: Two stacked panels of Drake. Top: recoiling, hand up — rejection. Bottom: smiling and pointing — approval.
when: Comparing two options where one is rejected and one is preferred. Slot 0 (top) = rejected, slot 1 (bottom) = chosen.

example.user_said: I read the docs once then immediately started guessing.

name: This Is Fine
scene: A cartoon dog sitting in a burning room sipping coffee. Slot 0 (top) sets up the disaster, slot 1 (bottom) is usually 'this is fine' or a variant of denial.
when: User describes a disaster but acts like it's normal. The contrast IS the joke.

example.user_said: Prod crashes every hour but nobody is paged so we're good.

name: X, X Everywhere
scene: Buzz Lightyear gestures broadly while telling Woody '[X], [X] everywhere'. Slot 0 is the noun alone, slot 1 is '[noun] everywhere'.
when: User keeps repeating the same theme/topic — call it out by saying it's everywhere.

example.user_said: Everyone at this conference will not shut up about agents.

name: Afraid to Ask Andy
scene: Andy from Parks & Rec, hands on cheeks, nervous. Slot 0 = an awkward admission of long-running ignorance, slot 1 = the absurd lengths to avoid asking.
when: User pretends to know a term/concept they have actually been faking for ages.

example.user_said: I've used Kubernetes for years, totally know what a sidecar is.
captions: still no idea what a sidecar is

name: Success Kid
scene: A baby with a clenched fist of victory. Tiny, petty wins celebrated like championships.
when: User celebrates a trivial accomplishment with disproportionate enthusiasm. Slot 0 = setup, slot 1 = the petty victory.

example.user_said: I remembered to put pants on before joining standup today.

name: Insanity Wolf
scene: Snarling black-and-white wolf. Slot 0 = a normal-ish setup, slot 1 = an unhinged escalation.
when: Take something the user said is mildly off and escalate it to a deranged extreme.

example.user_said: I sometimes skip the unit tests when I'm in a hurry.

name: Daily Struggle / Two Buttons
scene: Sweating man in a red shirt panicking between two red buttons. Slot 0 = button 1 label, slot 1 = button 2 label, slot 2 = the character (often the user identity or 'me' / 'devs').
when: User agonizes over a false choice between two options that are basically the same.

example.user_said: Should I quit or keep complaining on Twitter forever?

name: It's A Trap!
scene: Admiral Ackbar mid-yell. Slot 0 = setup (the bait), slot 1 = the trap warning.
when: User describes a transparent trap with zero awareness.

example.user_said: My boss said it'd be a quick 30-min call to discuss feedback.

name: Philosoraptor
scene: A velociraptor in The Thinker pose. Slot 0 = pseudo-philosophical setup, slot 1 = ironic punchline.
when: User asks a fake-deep or oddly profound-sounding question about something mundane.

example.user_said: If I name my variable better, does that make me a better person?
captions: if I name the variable better
do I become a better person

name: Xzibit Yo Dawg
scene: Xzibit smiling and gesturing. The classic recursion meme: 'Yo dawg, I heard you like X so I put X in your X so you can X while you X.' Slot 0 = first half (heard you like…), slot 1 = the recursion punchline.
when: Anything recursive, meta, or self-containing — model inside a model, framework wrapping a framework, AI roasting AI, function calling itself.

example.user_said: I've got an LLM evaluating outputs from another LLM.
captions: yo dawg, heard you like LLMs
so I put an LLM in your LLM

name: Galaxy Brain
scene: Four-panel escalation of a glowing brain getting more cosmic. Each slot = one rung on the increasingly-absurd ladder of supposed 'enlightenment'. Slot 0 = pedestrian, slot 3 = ascended/insane.
when: User climbs a ladder of bad reasoning where each step thinks it's smarter than the last. Perfect for galaxy-brained takes, recursive stacks of abstraction, or AI-on-AI-on-AI structures.

example.user_said: First we trained the model. Then we used it to label data. Then we trained another model on that. Then we let them critique each other.

name: Midwit
scene: Bell curve with three faces: a drooling brainlet on the left, an overthinking midwit in the middle, and a serene Jedi on the right. Both ends say the same simple thing; only the midwit overcomplicates. Slot 0 = brainlet take (left), slot 1 = midwit overcomplication (center), slot 2 = enlightened simple take (right).
when: User overcomplicates something the experienced and the naive both get right by instinct.

example.user_said: Just use sqlite. We added Kafka, two brokers, and an event store first.
captions: we need Kafka, brokers, an event store…

name: Spider-Man Pointing at Spider-Man
scene: Two Spider-Men pointing at each other. Slot 0 = label on Spider-Man A, slot 1 = label on Spider-Man B. Use when two things are accusing each other of being the thing.
when: Two duplicates accusing each other, indistinguishable rivals, or 'we're literally the same'.

example.user_said: They added a wrapper called "orchestrator" that does what the existing scheduler already did.

name: Gru's Plan
scene: Four panels of Gru presenting a flip-chart plan. First three panels: he reads the plan with confidence. Fourth panel: he double-takes at a flaw he just noticed. Slot 0-2 = three plan steps, slot 3 = same as slot 2 but now with the realization.
when: A plan that fully ignores its own obvious flaw on the last step.

example.user_said: We'll launch the model in beta, ship to all users, and the issues will surface in production.

name: Anakin and Padme
scene: 4-panel comic. Panel 1: Anakin says something earnestly. Panel 2: Padme smiles, '...for the better, right?' Panel 3: Anakin stares silently. Panel 4: Padme, now worried, '...right?' Slot 0 = Anakin's statement, slot 1 = Padme's hopeful affirmation, slot 2 = Anakin's silent reaction, slot 3 = Padme's worried follow-up. (Slot 4 sometimes empty / second-line filler.)
when: Innocent-sounding statement that turns dread-inducing as the user keeps not addressing the obvious problem.

example.user_said: I'm shipping the auth refactor today. We'll write the tests later.

name: Hide the Pain Harold
scene: An older man with a clearly-forced smile, eyes betraying suffering. Slot 0 = setup of the painful situation, slot 1 = the forced reaction.
when: User describes a quietly miserable situation with affected positivity.

example.user_said: Six hour cross-team meeting and I'm running it.

name: Disaster Girl
scene: A young girl smirking at the camera while a house burns behind her.
when: User caused a problem and is suspiciously calm about it.

example.user_said: I might have force-pushed to main but the build is still green.

name: Futurama Fry
scene: Fry from Futurama squinting suspiciously. Classic format: 'Not sure if X or just Y.'
when: User can't tell if a phenomenon is real or just their imagination/bias.

example.user_said: Is the model actually better or am I just used to its quirks?
captions: not sure if model is better
or just used to its quirks

name: Condescending Wonka
scene: Gene Wilder as Willy Wonka leaning on a hand, smiling sarcastically.
when: User says something self-important; throw it back at them mockingly.

example.user_said: We're disrupting the AI space with a new agent framework.
captions: do tell me how it disrupts AI

name: But That's None of My Business
scene: Kermit the Frog sipping tea, side-eye glance.
when: User passive-aggressively comments on someone else's mess. The roast: turn that judgment back on them.

example.user_said: Other team's PRs are always so messy.

name: Change My Mind
scene: Steven Crowder sitting at a folding table on a campus with a sign reading whatever caption you supply. Single slot = the bold/contrarian claim.
when: User makes a confident hot take.

example.user_said: TypeScript is just runtime errors with extra steps.
captions: TypeScript is runtime errors with extra steps

name: Stonks
scene: Wojak in a suit gesturing at a chart going UP, with the word 'STONKS' floating beside him.
when: Number going up despite the underlying logic being broken.

example.user_said: Latency tripled but somehow conversion's higher.

name: Roll Safe
scene: Man tapping his temple knowingly, as if to say 'big brain time'. Slot 0 = setup, slot 1 = the galaxy-brained false-logic conclusion.
when: User has bad logic that sounds smart on the surface.

example.user_said: Can't have a flaky test if you delete the test.

name: Doge
scene: Shiba Inu staring sideways. Multicolor text in Comic Sans typically reads 'much X', 'very Y', 'wow', 'such Z'.
when: Mock awe at something underwhelming. Caption like 'much X. very Y'.

example.user_said: We added another wrapper around the wrapper.

name: Bad Luck Brian
scene: School photo of an awkwardly-smiling kid in a sweater vest, braces, freckles. Two-line bad-fortune setup-then-payoff.
when: User did something well-intentioned and it backfired in a humiliating way.

example.user_said: I refactored the function and somehow broke production.

name: First World Problems
scene: Crying woman, mascara running. Caption: a setup of an extremely minor inconvenience.
when: User is dramatically upset about a comically minor inconvenience.

example.user_said: My laptop took 4 seconds to wake from sleep this morning.

name: Facepalm
scene: Captain Picard from Star Trek with his palm covering his face in disappointment.
when: User describes something obvious-in-hindsight that anyone could have prevented.

example.user_said: We deleted the only backup before testing the restore.

name: One Does Not Simply Walk Into Mordor
scene: Boromir from Fellowship gesturing solemnly. Slot 0 typically begins 'One does not simply', slot 1 = the supposedly easy thing the user thinks they can just do.
when: User describes a major undertaking like it's trivial.

example.user_said: We'll just migrate the whole monolith to microservices over the weekend.
captions: migrate a monolith over the weekend

name: Mocking Spongebob
scene: Spongebob in a chicken pose. Caption written in mocking AlTeRnAtInG cAsE — type the second slot exactly that way to get the full effect.
when: User said something pompous or naive; caricature it back at them.

example.user_said: I think AGI will be solved by next quarter.
captions: I think we'll have AGI by next quarter
i ThInK wE'lL hAvE aGi By NeXt QuArTeR

name: Kombucha Girl
scene: Two side-by-side reactions: left = enthusiastic interest, right = repulsed disgust. Same person, opposite faces.
when: User is oscillating between excitement and revulsion at the same idea.

example.user_said: I want to use Rust for everything but oh god the borrow checker.
captions: want to use Rust for everything

name: Conspiracy Keanu
scene: Keanu Reeves with a bewildered, what-if expression. Two-line setup ('What if…') then a conspiracy-flavored payoff.
when: User wades into 'what if it's all connected' territory.

example.user_said: What if all the bug reports are actually feature requests?

name: Schrute Facts
scene: Dwight Schrute from The Office, deadpan. Used for confidently-wrong corrections.
when: User confidently asserts something incorrect or pedantic.

example.user_said: Actually, Postgres is just MySQL with extra steps.

name: Cheems
scene: Two-panel comparison: a buff dog labeled with confident past behavior and a weak dog (Cheems) labeled with the user's diminished present. Slot 0 = past strength, slot 1 = current weakness.
when: User has lost their edge / contrast between past confidence and present capability.

example.user_said: In college I'd code 16 hours a day. Now I yawn at 9pm.

name: Why Not Both?
scene: A young girl gesturing happily, suggesting both options. Slot 0 = first option, slot 1 = second option, with the caption set up so 'why not both' is implied.
when: User is presenting a binary choice that doesn't have to be one.

example.user_said: Do I rewrite it in Go or Rust?
